title: Fourier concentration for bounded-width DNF
statement: Let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube that is represented by a disjunctive normal form of width at most the natural number $w$. For $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, the total squared Fourier weight of $f$, viewed as a real-valued function, on sets of coordinates of size strictly greater than $\lceil30w\lceil\log_2(3/\varepsilon)\rceil\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
$f$ has a DNF representation of width at most $w$
